recognize_zh: 鐵染色（Prussian blue）下，右側有核的紅血球母細胞周圍排列多顆藍綠色鐵顆粒，沿核周環繞一大段，是環狀鐵粒母細胞（ring sideroblast）；旁邊還有少數含零星藍色顆粒的無核紅血球（siderocyte）。
features: Nucleated erythroid precursors with red-counterstained nuclei surrounded by coarse blue-green iron granules
Granules arranged along the nuclear rim in a perinuclear (ring) distribution, qualifying as ring sideroblasts
Anucleate red cells containing a few scattered blue granules (siderocytes / Pappenheimer bodies)
Pale background red cells with some crenated forms
describe_en: Iron-stained smear (Prussian blue with red counterstain) shows several nucleated erythroid precursors containing coarse blue-green siderotic granules arranged around the nuclear rim, consistent with ring sideroblasts. Occasional anucleate red cells contain scattered iron granules (siderocytes). The image is focused on a thin area and quantitation cannot be performed from this field. Findings are consistent with ring sideroblasts; in the appropriate setting, ≥15% of erythroid precursors (or ≥5% with SF3B1 mutation) supports a ring sideroblast-associated myeloid neoplasm.

ddx.vs: Normal sideroblasts have only a few fine granules scattered randomly in the cytoplasm, not five or more granules encircling at least one-third of the nucleus.
Siderocytes are anucleate red cells with scattered granules, whereas ring sideroblasts are nucleated precursors with perinuclear granules.
Precipitate lies on top of cells and in the background in varying planes rather than being confined to the perinuclear cytoplasm of erythroblasts.
